leads.work: Gas flows at meters with no Sitara deal, or with a deal that has expired or doesn't cover every day. Volume Management (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, Charlotte Hawkins) emails Daren Farmer one meter at a time asking him to extend or create a deal. Until then the gas sits on 'strangers gas' and settlements can't pay counterparties.
leads.why: This comes up constantly from March to June 2000 and again in Jan 2001 ('Here I go again', 'I hate to be a pest'). Deals lapse because the evergreen flag isn't set or no new deal is referenced. Some threads run for months: Encina meter 6725 from March to May 2000, and Duke meters 6757 and 5192 for 1999 gas, with the customer calling settlements for payment. Allocation-close deadlines add pressure.

leads.work: When MIPS (measurement) gets incomplete data, it sends zero volumes to POPS. The zero overwrites the Gas Control estimate, so schedulers have to watch for it and override volumes in POPS by hand. Otherwise purchase expense lands in UA4 and the P&L is misstated.
leads.why: Messages call it an 'on-going problem' at various bidirectional meters. Measurement told the POPS team it was 'not a priority'. One meter was out of balance by more than 500,000 MMBtu month to date. The vendor (SPI) needed a work order. Manual overrides keep recurring (Enron Methanol meter 988291), and Brenda Herod escalated the measurement group's lack of accountability.

leads.work: Reconciling unaccounted-for gas (UA4) between the accounting systems and the pipeline balancing reports. This included a dedicated cross-team 'war room' for 1999 UA4, plus King Ranch scheduling and allocation cleanup.
leads.why: A full-time team of about 10 was pulled in for two weeks. March 2000 UA4 was 400,000+ MMBtu against a normal 100,000 or less. Rita Wynne hoped to 'prevent crisis modes like this from here on out'. Later corrections to MidTex/Tufco volumes also hit UA4.

leads.work: Every month, managers fill in an 'Hours' survey and an 'Activity driver' survey for the Operations Pricing Model, which allocates cost to commercial teams. The surveys go out on a schedule and Shari Mao and Brenda Herod follow up on late ones.
leads.why: Monthly spreadsheet surveys with tight deadlines. Managers 'expressed concerns on the process burdening' them and few responded on time. The surveys themselves say a standard report could replace them ('This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month').

leads.work: EnronOnline weekday-only (24x5 / WkD) products don't bridge to Sitara. Each such deal fails in the bridge monitor and has to be keyed into Sitara by hand as separate Monday–Friday strips, then cleared from the monitor. Other failed EOL deals are also booked manually.
leads.why: Scott Mills, Dale Neuner, Jennifer Denny and Brenda Herod all describe the manual entry. 'An effort... has not been started' to fix the bridge, and paths with open-ended end dates add more reconciling items. Torrey Moorer faxed failed deals for manual booking.

leads.work: PG&E Texas / PGEV interconnect and contract volume variances, plus double scheduling on ENA and HPL with a desk-to-desk deal. Settlements (Sherlyn Schumack) chases scheduling by email, fax and voicemail, and manual line items get added to invoices.
leads.why: Issues run from February to June 2000 and were unresolved for months ('sent several emails, faxed... no updates'). A meeting recap set up a daily variance process. Daren asked legal to transfer the ENA transport contracts to HPL, which would remove the duplicate scheduling and allocation. The items also feed the intercompany cleanup before the SAP go-live.

leads.work: Setting up ENA↔HPL desk-to-desk deals each month at certain meters (e.g. meter 378) so volumes can be allocated before close.
leads.why: Requested repeatedly for February and March 2000 with urgent same-day deadlines ('bridge will close today'). Aimee asked to create it 'March going forward'.

leads.work: Price and deal discrepancies between Sitara/Unify and counterparty invoices: wrong price, wrong counterparty, deals missing on the counterparty side. Settlements and client services ask the trader or Daren to fix them, often after many follow-ups.
leads.why: Examples: Mitchell (HSC -0.05 vs -0.04); PanEnergy exchange, where a pricing fix requested in April was still being chased through June and there was a 'massive A/R issue'; Midcon invoices for about $350K unpaid; GMT paid to the wrong company; Aspect on the wrong Sitara number; Williams billing HPL deals on the ENA invoice.

leads.work: Producers and customers send nominations and revisions by email (KCS Josey Ranch revisions, Reliant egmnom spreadsheets, Calpine daily nom, EOG, Walter O&G, Lyondell, ExxonMobil fuel needs, Enron Methanol/MTBE monthly). These are forwarded around and re-keyed into Sitara/MOPS/Unify. Cuts reported by Oasis/El Paso are also entered by hand as estimates.
leads.why: The same formats recur several times a month: 1st, 2nd and 3rd revisions to the Josey nom, monthly estimates, and plain forwards to the logistics list. Volumes are typed in by hand ('I've made the change in my spreadsheet'; 'I will enter in MOPS as estimates').

leads.work: Building monthly nomination and volume estimates for customers (Entex, Southern Union, Tufco, Calpine) by hand, e.g. averaging the last three months.
leads.why: Ami Chokshi sends Daren a series of one-line estimate emails each bid week, some built by simple averaging. This looks easy to template.

leads.work: Every month, wellhead spot purchases are emailed by Vance Taylor as tables and then entered into Sitara as deal tickets by Tom Acton.
leads.why: A tabular email gets re-keyed into Sitara each month, and some tickets don't flow on to MOPS.

leads.work: Each month, transport usage tickets are refreshed by hand with matrix and third-party rates, and volumes are zeroed for schedulers to re-enter.
leads.why: Heidi Withers spent two days updating all the pipes for June and asked schedulers to check every pipe's volumes in Position Manager. She then ran a Basis Adjustment report to double-check the rates.

leads.work: Plant upset and outage broadcasts (Methanol, MTBE, Clear Lake methanol, pipeline outages) sent to long distribution lists, each followed by nomination and scheduling changes.
leads.why: Many near-identical status emails, each of which can change the gas volumes needed.

leads.work: Collecting monthly vacation schedules and sending out-of-office coverage emails and weekend on-call notes.
leads.why: Recurring requests from the admin to 'submit your vacation by…', plus repeated coverage and on-call emails, some sent twice with corrections.

leads.work: Monthly finance review cycle: O&M reports, preliminary ledgers, allocation-percentage reviews, and labor distribution reports that sometimes don't reach the managers who need them.
leads.why: Monthly deadlines for review and changes, broken spreadsheets ('errors in every cell'), a manager who wasn't getting his labor report, a departed employee still charged to his RC, workorders set up wrongly, and IT charges missing for two months.

leads.work: Building the Unify/Sitara enhancement list with estimated hours saved for each item.
leads.why: This is management's own exercise to quantify where the systems waste time (transport contracting, hourly transactions, the shipper imbalance worksheet, consolidated UA4 tracking). It is a direct pointer to known pain points.

leads.work: Contract administration chasing: terminations, routing for signatures, pipeline name corrections, and counterparty or contract changes in Global/Sitara that ripple into Unify re-pathing.
leads.why: Marlene Hilliard repeatedly chased a contract held since April and asked about deals before terminating contracts. A new feature for changing counterparties brought warnings about corrupting Unify paths and extra steps for schedulers.

leads.work: Storage and Bammel bookkeeping: Cilco storage variances against confirmed volumes, PMA revised schedules, and storage purchase entry and payment coordination.
leads.why: Cilco withdrew 200,000 MMBtu more than was booked because there was no process for communicating changes. PMAs are revised for several months at once, and a $2.4M payment needed deal entry, scheduling and reminders across many people.

leads.work: Meters that are over-nominated or nominated without being allocatable, which distort the P&L and risk numbers and show up on error reports (Revenue Volume Comparison).
leads.why: Meter 1591 was nominated at 1,000/d since 1999 but flowed almost nothing. Check meters show volumes in MOPS that don't bridge to POPS. Error-report exceptions are cleared one meter at a time.

leads.work: Ad hoc data pulls and research for management: ENA sales on HPL, HPL buy/sell reports, unmetered gas loss explanations, and the controls/standards assessment.
leads.why: There were several rounds of Sitara reports and manual counterparty lists. The gas-loss review asked for an explanation of every volume. Each controls template needed detailed listing and measurement work.

leads.work: Performance review (PEP) logistics: picking reviewers, collecting them by email when the system was down, and a PRC meeting that ran into the evening.
leads.why: Mid-year and year-end cycles; one PRC meeting ran from 1pm to almost midnight. When PEP failed, reviewer lists were emailed and entered by hand by the helpdesk.

leads.work: Planning the annual customer appreciation trip: guest lists, invitations and RSVPs gathered through spreadsheets and email.
leads.why: Many deadlines and a consolidation spreadsheet run by an assistant. This is the 8th annual meeting, so it recurs every year.
